title: Latency + Network Signal Fusion for Region & Variant Failover Arbiter
creator: Riya Patel
description: Problem: Region selection currently relies on either simple latency heuristics or coarse availability signals. We need a single arbiter that fuses p50/p95 latency telemetry with network health signals (packet loss, retransmits, connection errors) to choose POP/region and to decide graceful fallback to model variants (smaller context / quantized). Goals: reduce tail user latency and improve availability during transient network degradations without causing oscillation or unnecessary model downgrades.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Composite net-health score computed per POP every minute and visible in Console grafana panel. 2) Router uses score to prioritize POPs and triggers variant fallback when score < 30 for > 2 consecutive minutes. 3) New scoring respects cooldowns and sample minimums to avoid flapping. 4) Canary rollout: staging -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback automation. 5) Integration tests and chaos tests validate behavior under packet loss and p95 spikes.
implementation_notes: Architecture: implement a telemetry consumer job (kafka -> processing) that computes per-pop minute rollups for p50, p95, packet_loss, connection_error_rate. Scoring function: normalized_z = zscore(p50,p95,loss) -> weighted sum: w_p95=0.6, w_p50=0.2, w_loss=0.2 -> map to 0..100. Apply temporal EWMA smoothing (alpha=0.3). Hysteresis: require score cross below threshold for N consecutive windows (N=2) before triggering variant fallback. Safety: require minimum sample count (>=200 requests/min) and fallback only if latency degradation correlates with increased packet loss or error rate. Routing integration: expose score as 'net_health' to region-decider; route policies accept 'prefer' thresholds per tier (tier-1 require >60, tier-2 >40).
decisions: Score computed server-side in control plane to centralize policy and avoid divergence from edge.
Chosen weights favor p95 to prioritize tail latency over median.
Use EWMA for smoothing to balance reactivity vs. stability.
Fallback to variant is model-agnostic: label variant via model catalog (e.g., m-7b-quantized) and require verified compatibility mapping.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and normalization. Integration: deploy to staging and run synthetic traffic patterns (normal, p95 spike, packet loss injection). Chaos: simulate inter-pop packet_loss and partial network partition. Observability: dashboard with heatmap of net_health over POPs, alert when scoring algorithm triggers fallback in canary. End-to-end test: issue traffic through API and assert requests are served by fallback variant when net_health < threshold.
rollout_plan: Stage: deploy scoring service in staging and enable read-only view for 1 week. Canary: enable routing influence for 10% of traffic in us-east-1 -> monitor latency, error rates for 48h -> expand to 50% then 100%. Automated rollback if customer_error_rate increases by >1% or p95 increases by >20% vs baseline. Run a 2-week validation window before enabling for Dedicated customers.
